# Tools

moodle-mcp has **266 tools**, 265 at the default privacy level. This page is generated from the server itself, so it lists them exactly as your AI app gets them, with the descriptions the agent reads. You don't call tools yourself: you ask in your own words, and the agent picks them.

In the tables, ✓ marks the tools you still get with each limit: **Read only** with [read-only access](../limits.md#read-only), **Teacher** and **Student** with each [role](../limits.md#your-role). Read-only access leaves out every tool that changes something in Moodle (a grade, a post, an activity, an attempt); session tools, such as logging in or showing the browser, are always there, and so are `download_file` and `export_grades`, which only save a file on your computer.

### `login` {#login}

**Log in to Moodle**

Make sure there is a Moodle session. If there is one, returns the logged-in user at once. Otherwise opens a browser window at the site's login page and waits until the person logs in there themselves (the server never sees their password), then returns the user. Call it when another tool reports a missing or expired session.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `timeoutSeconds` |  | integer | How long to wait for the person to log in, in seconds (default 300) |

</details>

### `logout` {#logout}

**Log out of Moodle**

End the person's Moodle session in the server's browser, so someone else can log in (another account: login opens the window again). Only Moodle's session ends: a single sign-on provider may keep its own and log the same person back in. Only when the person asks.

*No inputs.*

### `get_me` {#get-me}

**Who am I**

Tell who the logged-in person is: user id, username, full name, email, language, time zone, first and last access, and the site. With courseId, also their roles in that course and whether they can edit it and grade in it.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` |  | integer | A course id (from list_courses) to also get the person's roles and abilities there |

</details>

### `get_site_info` {#get-site-info}

**Get the Moodle site's info**

What the Moodle site says about itself: its name, URL, language, how people log in (its own form, guest access, single sign-on providers) and whether it's in maintenance; readable before logging in. With courseId, also the activity and resource types the person can add to that course (none if they can't edit it): take the type for create_activity from here. Moodle shows its version only to administrators, so it isn't given.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` |  | integer | A course to list the activity types that can be added to it |

</details>

### `configure` {#configure}

**Configure the server**

Set this server's configuration for this session: the Moodle site (url; a new one is added to the server's sites and kept, a known one becomes active, see use_site), whether the browser runs without a window (headless), how student tools view and do things (trail) and the browser profile folder (profileDir). It can also narrow the kinds of tools (scopes), the role (role) or access to read only (access) and tighten how others' data reaches you (studentData), never the other way: widening is the person's, in the client's configuration. Each is optional; only those given change. The URL is checked to be a Moodle site. Kept in memory only, but for a new site, which stays among the server's sites. Returns the effective configuration, as server_info.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `url` |  | string | The Moodle site's URL, or any page of it (a course URL works: the site is read from it) |
| `headless` |  | boolean | Run the browser without a window (logging in always shows one) |
| `trail` |  | `realistic`, `fast` | How student tools view and do things: realistic (real pages, human pace; Moodle logs views and completion) or fast |
| `profileDir` |  | string | Absolute folder for the browser profile that keeps the Moodle session; outside the server's folder |
| `scopes` |  | string | Narrow the kinds of tools for this session: a profile (teacher, student, content) or scopes (content, student-data, grading, communication, as-student, browser). Only fewer than now, never more |
| `studentData` |  | `block`, `pseudonymize`, `clear` | Tighten how others' data reaches you for this session (block is strictest). Only stricter than now, never looser |
| `role` |  | `all`, `teacher`, `student` | Keep only one role's tools for this session (teacher or student), from all; never back to all |
| `access` |  | `read`, `write` | read: keep only the tools that change nothing in Moodle for this session; never back to write |

</details>

### `show_browser` {#show-browser}

**Show or hide the browser**

Show the browser to the person, so they can watch what the tools do: the window opens now (the session is kept) and each tool brings the Moodle page it works on to the front. Or hide it again: the window closes and tools go on without one. Only when the person asks to watch or to stop watching. Open tabs don't survive the switch; what was saved in Moodle does. Changes nothing in Moodle.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `visible` | ✅ | boolean | true to show the browser and follow the tools in it, false to hide it |

</details>

### `server_info` {#server-info}

**Server info**

Show this server's version and effective configuration: the active Moodle site and the others, the browser profile folder, the browser, and where each setting came from. Contains no secrets. Does not open the browser.

*No inputs.*

### `list_sites` {#list-sites}

**List the Moodle sites**

List the Moodle sites this server knows, by name: their URL, which one is active (every other tool works on it) and whether each comes from the person's configuration or was added at run time. Switch with use_site.

*No inputs.*

### `add_site` {#add-site}

**Add a Moodle site**

Add a Moodle site to this server, kept for later sessions: its URL (any page of it works) and, optionally, a short name (letters, digits, dots, hyphens; its host by default). Without url, the person is asked for both in their app, where the client can ask them (MCP elicitation); else ask them yourself. Two accounts on one site are two sites: add the second with a name of its own. It doesn't become active: switch to it with use_site, and log in there when a tool asks. Only when the person asks for another site.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `url` |  | string | The site's URL, or any page of it; without it, the person is asked in their app when it can |
| `name` |  | string | A short name for it; its host by default |

</details>

### `use_site` {#use-site}

**Switch to another Moodle site**

Make another known site the active one, by name (list_sites): every other tool works on it from now on. The previous site's browser closes and keeps its session; if the new one has none, the next tool asks to log in. Tell the person which site you're now working on. Lasts for this session.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `name` | ✅ | string | The site's name, as list_sites gives it |

</details>

### `remove_site` {#remove-site}

**Remove a Moodle site**

Forget a site added at run time, by name, and delete its browser profile with its session. Not the active site (switch first) nor one from the person's configuration (they remove it there). Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `name` | ✅ | string | The site's name, as list_sites gives it |

</details>

### `list_courses` {#list-courses}

**List my courses**

List the Moodle courses the logged-in person is enrolled in (as teacher or student), with their ids, names, category, URL, visibility, dates and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's progress: only as a student, in courses with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' progress is in get_completion_report). Filter by dates with classification.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `classification` |  | `all`, `inprogress`, `future`, `past` | Which courses by their dates: "all" (default), "inprogress", "future" or "past" |

</details>

### `get_course_structure` {#get-course-structure}

**Get a course's structure**

Get a Moodle course's sections and activities: ids, names, types, URLs, visibility, whether the person can open each one, restrictions and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's completion: only as a student, on activities with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' completion is in get_completion_report). With details, also each activity's dates and restriction text as the course page shows them. Takes the course id from list_courses.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `details` |  | boolean | Also read the course page for each activity's dates and restriction text (slower; default false) |

</details>

### `get_activity_content` {#get-activity-content}

**Read an activity's content**

Read a content activity as a person would, so Moodle logs the view: a page's or label's text, a book's chapters, a URL resource's target, or a file resource's or folder's files (as links). Takes the id and type from get_course_structure. With the realistic trail it reads page by page at a reader's pace and reports progress.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `type` | ✅ | `page`, `book`, `label`, `url`, `resource`, `folder` | The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `get_activity_settings` {#get-activity-settings}

**Get an activity's settings**

Read every setting of an activity as its edit form holds them, without changing anything: its module, name, description, each field with its form name, label, value and options, a resource's, folder's or SCORM's files, and its access restrictions and completion in the terms update_activity takes. Use it before update_activity. Teachers only. Takes the activity id from get_course_structure.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `download_file` {#download-file}

**Download a file from Moodle**

Save a file of the Moodle site to a local folder, with the person's session: a resource's or folder's file (get_activity_content), an assignment's brief file or submitted file (get_assignment, get_submissions), a forum attachment (get_discussion). Only URLs of the configured site's host (its media too: videos it serves outside Moodle); external links (YouTube…) are for other tools. Never overwrites: an existing name gets a number. Returns where it was saved.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `url` | ✅ | string | The file's URL on the site, as the other tools give it (…/pluginfile.php/…) |
| `destDir` | ✅ | string | Absolute local folder to save into; created if missing |

</details>

### `create_activity` {#create-activity}

**Create an activity or resource**

Create an activity or resource of any type (page, label, url, resource, folder, assign, quiz, forum…) at the end of a section, through Moodle's own form, hidden from students by default. Common fields have their own inputs, access restrictions and completion included; any other setting goes in settings by its form field name. files are local paths uploaded to a file resource or folder, or a SCORM's package (type scorm, the first file). Returns the new activity's id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `sectionId` | ✅ | integer | The section's id, as get_course_structure gives it |
| `type` | ✅ | string | Moodle's module name: page, label, url, resource, folder, assign, quiz, forum, book… |
| `name` |  | string | Required except for labels |
| `files` |  | string list | Absolute local paths: a file resource's file (the first is the main one), a folder's files, a SCORM's package (.zip) |
| `toolId` |  | integer | type lti: the external tool it's made from, as list_external_tools gives it (Moodle 5 makes LTI activities only from a tool) |
| `description` |  | string | The description (HTML), shown on the activity's page |
| `content` |  | string | A page's content, or a label's text (HTML) |
| `url` |  | string | A URL resource's target |
| `visibility` |  | `shown`, `hidden`, `stealth` | "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link, where the site allows it |
| `restrictions` |  | object | When students can open it (&#123; conditions: [] &#125; removes them) |
| `completion` |  | object | When it counts as complete |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |
| `settings` |  | object | Any other form field by its name in Moodle's activity form, e.g. &#123;"duedate[enabled]": true, "duedate[day]": 12, "grade[modgrade_point]": 10&#125; |

</details>

### `update_activity` {#update-activity}

**Update an activity's settings or content**

Change an existing activity through Moodle's own form: name, description, a page's or label's content, a URL's target, visibility, access restrictions, completion, a file resource's or folder's files (add, remove by their path as get_activity_settings lists them, or replace all), a SCORM's package (replaced in place: the activity keeps its id, settings and grade item; attempts stay in the SCOs the new package keeps, by their identifier, and go with the SCOs it drops), or any other setting by its form field name in settings. Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure, and a SCORM as get_scorm reads it after a new package. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `description` |  | string | The description (HTML), shown on the activity's page |
| `content` |  | string | A page's content, or a label's text (HTML) |
| `url` |  | string | A URL resource's target |
| `visibility` |  | `shown`, `hidden`, `stealth` | "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link, where the site allows it |
| `restrictions` |  | object | When students can open it (&#123; conditions: [] &#125; removes them) |
| `completion` |  | object | When it counts as complete |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |
| `settings` |  | object | Any other form field by its name in Moodle's activity form, e.g. &#123;"duedate[enabled]": true, "duedate[day]": 12, "grade[modgrade_point]": 10&#125; |
| `files` |  | object | A file resource's or folder's files; untouched when missing |
| `package` |  | string | A SCORM's new package: an absolute local path to a .zip, replacing the current one in place |

</details>

### `validate_html` {#validate-html}

**Check HTML before sending it to Moodle**

Check HTML for a page, a label, a description or a post before sending it, without Moodle, and approximately: only Moodle knows exactly what its cleaning keeps. Reports, with their lines, parse errors and tags left open, what Moodle's cleaning removes (scripts, styles, frames, forms, event attributes such as onclick, javascript: links), files the HTML names that are neither URLs nor in embed, and embed files that don't exist or the HTML doesn't name. Give embed as you would to the content tool.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `text` |  | string | The HTML |
| `file` |  | string | Or an absolute path to a local HTML file |
| `embed` |  | string list | The local files you'll embed, as the content tools take them |

</details>

### `edit_activity` {#edit-activity}

**Move, rename, show or hide an activity**

Move an activity to another section (at its end) or before another activity, to reorder a course; rename it; or set its visibility ("shown", "hidden", or "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link). Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `visibility` |  | `shown`, `hidden`, `stealth` |  |
| `sectionId` |  | integer | Move it to the end of this section |
| `beforeActivityId` |  | integer | Move it before this activity (in that activity's section) |

</details>

### `duplicate_activity` {#duplicate-activity}

**Duplicate an activity**

Duplicate an activity right after itself, with its settings and content (not participants' data). Returns the copy's id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `delete_activity` {#delete-activity}

**Delete an activity**

Delete an activity from a course, with its participants' data (submissions, attempts, posts, grades). Destructive: confirm with the person first, naming the activity.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `activityId` | ✅ | integer | The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `add_section` {#add-section}

**Add a section**

Add a section to a course, at the end or after a given section, optionally named and described. Returns its id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `summary` |  | string | Its description (HTML) |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |
| `afterSectionId` |  | integer | Add it after this section; at the end when missing |

</details>

### `edit_section` {#edit-section}

**Edit a section**

Change a section: rename it, describe it, show or hide it (with its activities), restrict access to it, or move it after another section. Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `sectionId` | ✅ | integer | A section's id (not its number), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `visible` |  | boolean |  |
| `summary` |  | string | Its description (HTML) |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |
| `restrictions` |  | object | When students can open it (&#123; conditions: [] &#125; removes them) |
| `afterSectionId` |  | integer | Move it after this section |

</details>

### `delete_section` {#delete-section}

**Delete a section**

Delete a section and every activity in it, with their participants' data. Destructive: confirm with the person first, saying which activities go with it.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |
| `sectionId` | ✅ | integer | A section's id (not its number), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `update_course` {#update-course}

**Update a course's settings**

Change a course's full name, short name, summary (HTML) or any other setting by its field name in Moodle's course settings form (settings), through that form. Only what is given changes. Returns the course afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `fullName` |  | string |  |
| `shortName` |  | string |  |
| `summary` |  | string | HTML |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |
| `settings` |  | object | Other fields by their name in the course settings form, e.g. &#123;"visible": 0, "startdate[day]": 1&#125; |

</details>

### `list_book_chapters` {#list-book-chapters}

**List a book's chapters**

List a book's chapters in order: id, title, whether each is a subchapter or hidden, and its place; with content, each chapter's HTML and images too (one page read per chapter, logged by Moodle as a view). A teacher sees hidden chapters, a student doesn't. The chapter ids are what the other book tools take.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `content` |  | boolean | Also each chapter's HTML and images |

</details>

### `add_book_chapter` {#add-book-chapter}

**Add a chapter to a book**

Add a chapter to a book through Moodle's chapter form: its title and content (HTML, with local images embedded), at the end or after another chapter, as a subchapter of the chapter before it if asked, hidden if asked (shown by default, as Moodle adds it: hide it while the book is visible and the chapter isn't ready). Returns the new chapter's id and the chapters. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `title` | ✅ | string |  |
| `content` | ✅ | string | Its content (HTML); Moodle requires some |
| `subchapter` |  | boolean | A subchapter of the chapter before it (not for the first) |
| `hidden` |  | boolean | Hidden from students |
| `afterChapterId` |  | integer | The chapter it goes after; at the end without it |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the content, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |

</details>

### `edit_book_chapter` {#edit-book-chapter}

**Change a book's chapter**

Change a chapter's title, content (HTML, with local images embedded) or whether it is a subchapter, through its form: only what is given changes. move_book_chapter moves it, set_book_chapter_visibility shows or hides it. Returns the chapters afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `chapterId` | ✅ | integer | The chapter's id, as list_book_chapters gives it |
| `title` |  | string |  |
| `content` |  | string |  |
| `subchapter` |  | boolean |  |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the content, which names each by its file name: &#60;img src="shot.png"&#62; |

</details>

### `move_book_chapter` {#move-book-chapter}

**Move a book's chapter up or down**

Move a chapter one place up or down, as the table of contents' arrows do: a chapter moves with its subchapters, past the whole chapter before or after it; a subchapter moves alone. Call it again to move further. Returns the chapters afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `chapterId` | ✅ | integer | The chapter's id, as list_book_chapters gives it |
| `direction` | ✅ | `up`, `down` |  |

</details>

### `set_book_chapter_visibility` {#set-book-chapter-visibility}

**Show or hide a book's chapter**

Show a chapter to students or hide it from them, as the table of contents' eye does: a chapter's subchapters go with it, and a subchapter of a hidden chapter stays hidden. Returns the chapters afterwards. Changes what students see: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `chapterId` | ✅ | integer | The chapter's id, as list_book_chapters gives it |
| `visible` | ✅ | boolean |  |

</details>

### `delete_book_chapter` {#delete-book-chapter}

**Delete a book's chapter**

Delete a chapter with its files; deleting a chapter (not a subchapter) deletes its subchapters too. Returns the chapters afterwards. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bookId` | ✅ | integer | The book's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `get_lesson_pages` {#get-lesson-pages}

**Read a lesson's pages as its teacher**

Read a lesson's pages as its teacher has them in Moodle's lesson editor, in order: type (content, a question type, cluster, end of cluster, end of branch), title, contents, and a content page's buttons or a question's answers with their responses, scores and jumps (a page's id, or next-page, end-of-lesson…). Takes a teacher's role; a student plays a lesson with get_lesson_page.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `lessonId` | ✅ | integer | The lesson's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |

</details>

### `add_lesson_page` {#add-lesson-page}

**Add a page to a lesson**

Add a page to a lesson through Moodle's lesson editor: a content page with its buttons, a question page (multichoice, truefalse, shortanswer, numerical, matching, essay) with its answers, responses, scores and jumps, or a cluster, end of cluster or end of branch; after a page, or last. A jump to a page the lesson doesn't have is refused before anything is saved, so add the pages first and set their jumps after with edit_lesson_page when they point forward. Returns the new page's id and the lesson's page ids in order. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `lessonId` | ✅ | integer | The lesson's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `type` | ✅ | `content`, `multichoice`, `truefalse`, `shortanswer`, `numerical`, `matching`, `essay`, `cluster`, `end-of-cluster`, `end-of-branch` |  |
| `title` |  | string |  |
| `contents` |  | string | The page's contents (HTML); local files it names (&#60;img src="shot.png"&#62;) go in embed |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files to embed in the contents, answers or responses |
| `buttons` |  | object list | A content page's buttons, in order; given, they replace them all |
| `answers` |  | object list | A question page's answers, in order (given, they replace them all); an essay or structural page's single row |
| `multipleAnswers` |  | boolean | Multichoice: more than one answer can be right |
| `caseSensitive` |  | boolean | Short answer: answers compared case-sensitively |
| `fields` |  | object | Any other field of the page's form, by name (layout, display…) |
| `after` |  | integer | The page it goes after (0: first); last without it |

</details>

### `edit_lesson_page` {#edit-lesson-page}

**Change a lesson's page**

Change a lesson's page through its form in the lesson editor: title, contents, buttons or answers (given, they replace them all), options and other fields; only what is given changes, and a page keeps its type. A jump to a page the lesson doesn't have is refused before anything is saved. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

| `title` |  | string |  |
| `contents` |  | string | The page's contents (HTML); local files it names (&#60;img src="shot.png"&#62;) go in embed |
| `embed` |  | string list | Absolute local files to embed in the contents, answers or responses |
| `buttons` |  | object list | A content page's buttons, in order; given, they replace them all |
| `answers` |  | object list | A question page's answers, in order (given, they replace them all); an essay or structural page's single row |
| `multipleAnswers` |  | boolean | Multichoice: more than one answer can be right |
| `caseSensitive` |  | boolean | Short answer: answers compared case-sensitively |
| `fields` |  | object | Any other field of the page's form, by name (layout, display…) |

</details>

### `move_lesson_page` {#move-lesson-page}

**Move a lesson's page**

Move a lesson's page after another (0: first), as the lesson editor's move link does. Jumps by page id still lead to the same pages; next-page and previous-page follow the new order. Returns the page ids in order. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

Add a field to a database activity through Moodle's form for its type: text, textarea, number, date, menu, radiobutton, checkbox, multimenu, url, file, picture or latlong, with a name unique in the database, a description, whether it's required (not for a date), and the type's settings. | `name` | ✅ | string |  |
| `description` |  | string |  |
| `required` |  | boolean |  |
| `options` |  | object | The type's settings; each type takes only its own |

</details>

**Change a database's field**

Change a database field's name, description, whether it's required, or its type's settings (one by one): what is left out stays. Renaming it renames its tag in the templates, as Moodle does. Its type can't change: delete it and add another. Returns the fields. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| `name` |  | string |  |
| `description` |  | string |  |

| `options` |  | object | The type's settings; each type takes only its own |

</details>

Delete a database field: what every entry has in it goes too, and its tags leave the templates. Returns the fields. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

| Input | Required | Type | Description |

**Set a database's template**

Save one of a database's templates as given, without Moodle's HTML editor in between: list (repeated per entry, between listHeader and listFooter), single, add (the entry form: each field's tag once), search, rss, rssTitle, css or js. Fields go in as [[name]], Moodle's other tags as ##tag## (##edit##, ##delete##, ##more##, ##user##…). reset: true puts back Moodle's default. Returns every template. </details>

## Course life cycle {#lifecycle}

| Tool | Description | Read only | Teacher | Student |
| --- | --- | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| [`copy_course`](#copy-course) | Copy a course |  | ✓ |  |
| [`backup_course`](#backup-course) | Back up a course |  | ✓ |  |
| [`restore_course`](#restore-course) | Restore a course backup |  | ✓ |  |
| [`read_backup`](#read-backup) | Read what a backup file holds | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| [`anonymize_backup`](#anonymize-backup) | Anonymize a backup file | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| [`import_activities`](#import-activities) | Import activities from another course |  | ✓ |  |
| [`reset_course`](#reset-course) | Reset a course for a new year |  | ✓ |  |
| [`copy_between_sites`](#copy-between-sites) | Copy course content to another site |  | ✓ |  |

### `copy_course` {#copy-course}

**Copy a course**

Copy a course into a new one, as Moodle's "Copy course" does: its content (and, with withUsers, its people's enrolments and data) under a new full and short name, in a category (the course's unless given), with new dates. Needs the rights to back up, restore and create courses. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Creates a course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `fullName` | ✅ | string |  |
| `shortName` | ✅ | string |  |
| `categoryId` |  | integer |  |
| `start` |  | string | The new course's start, ISO 8601 |
| `end` |  | string | The new course's end, ISO 8601 |
| `withUsers` |  | boolean | Also its participants and their data (default false) |
| `visible` |  | boolean |  |

</details>

### `backup_course` {#backup-course}

**Back up a course**

Back a course up to a .mbz file in a local folder, through Moodle's backup wizard: its content, and with withUsers its people's data too (anonymize makes their names anonymous). Or only some of it: sections (each with everything in it) and activities, never with people's data, and the file naming no one and no site unless anonymous is false. Moodle keeps a copy in the course's backup area. Restore it with restore_course, on this site or another. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `destDir` | ✅ | string | An absolute local folder for the file |
| `withUsers` |  | boolean | Also its participants' data (default false) |
| `anonymize` |  | boolean | With users: Moodle makes their names and contact data anonymous |
| `sections` |  | integer list | Only these sections, by id (get_course_structure), each with everything in it |
| `activities` |  | integer list | Only these activities and resources, by course module id |
| `anonymous` |  | boolean | The file names no person and no site or course of origin: true by default for sections or activities, false for a whole course |

</details>

### `restore_course` {#restore-course}

**Restore a course backup**

Restore a .mbz backup through Moodle's restore wizard: into a new course in a category (no intoCourseId), or into an existing course, adding to its content (mode merge, the default) or replacing it (replace deletes the course's content first). Merged into a course, sectionId puts every restored activity at the end of that section, and afterSectionId the backup's sections as new ones after that one; the result names the new sections and activities, and warnings what was left broken (restrictions or links to what wasn't restored) for the person to fix. A new course takes the backup's names unless fullName and shortName are given. A backup from a newer Moodle, or with activity types this site doesn't offer, is refused. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Changes Moodle, and replace can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `file` | ✅ | string | The backup's absolute local path (.mbz) |
| `intoCourseId` |  | integer | An existing course to restore into; a new course when missing |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | For a new course: its category |
| `mode` |  | `merge`, `replace` | Into an existing course: add to it (default) or replace its content |
| `fullName` |  | string |  |
| `shortName` |  | string |  |
| `withUsers` |  | boolean | Restore the participants' data the backup has (default false) |
| `sectionId` |  | integer | Merged into a course: every restored activity at the end of this section |
| `afterSectionId` |  | integer | Merged into a course: the backup's sections as new sections after this one |

</details>

### `read_backup` {#read-backup}

**Read what a backup file holds**

Read a Moodle backup file (.mbz) on this computer without restoring it, without Moodle: the Moodle that made it, the original site and course, its sections and activities (the original site's ids), the plugins a site needs to restore it, whether it holds people's data or the gradebook, what each activity refers to that the backup doesn't hold (restrictions on activities left out, links to them, its grade category), which a restore elsewhere leaves broken, and what in it still names a person, the site or the course. Use it before restore_course or before sharing a backup.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `file` | ✅ | string | An absolute local path to the .mbz file |

</details>

### `anonymize_backup` {#anonymize-backup}

**Anonymize a backup file**

Write a copy of a Moodle backup file (.mbz) that names no one and no site, on this computer, without Moodle: every user id 0, authors' names empty, the original site's address, the course's id and names and the backup's log replaced by neutral values; the content (texts, settings, files) as it was. Moodle restores it as a backup from another site. Refused for a backup with people's data (Moodle's own anonymize makes those). Returns what was cleared. For sharing a unit with other teachers.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `file` | ✅ | string | An absolute local path to the .mbz file |
| `destFile` | ✅ | string | Where to write the copy (an absolute local path; it may be file itself) |

</details>

### `import_activities` {#import-activities}

**Import activities from another course**

Import activities from another course into a course, as Moodle's "Import" does: all of them, or only activityIds, with their sections, never people's data. Returns the new activities' ids. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `fromCourseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `toCourseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `activityIds` |  | integer list | Only these activities of the other course (course module ids) |

</details>

### `reset_course` {#reset-course}

**Reset a course for a new year**

Reset a course as Moodle's reset form does: delete only what's named in delete (submissions, attempts, posts, grades… in every activity that has them), unenrol the people with unenrolRoles, move the start date (and the activities' dates with it), and set any other field of the form by name. Nothing is deleted unless named. Can't be undone: confirm every item with the person first. Returns Moodle's report.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `delete` |  | object |  |
| `unenrolRoles` |  | integer list | Role ids whose people are unenrolled |
| `start` |  | string | The new start date, ISO 8601 |
| `fields` |  | object | Any other field of the reset form, by name |

</details>

### `copy_between_sites` {#copy-between-sites}

**Copy course content to another site**

Copy a course's content from one of this server's sites to another (list_sites): some activities (activityIds), some sections with everything in them (sectionIds), or, with neither, the whole course. Through Moodle's backup on the first site and its restore on the second, never with people's data and naming no one; the file stays on this computer, never passes through you, and is deleted after. It goes into an existing course (toCourseId): at the end of one of its sections (toSectionId), or, for sections, as new ones after toAfterSectionId; a whole course can go into a new course in a category instead (toCategoryId). Returns what was created, and warnings for what was left broken (restrictions or links to what wasn't copied) for the person to fix. Each site needs a session (use_site, then login). The active site stays the same. Within one site, use import_activities or copy_course. It can take minutes. Changes the target site: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `fromSite` | ✅ | string | A site's name, as list_sites gives it |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course to copy from, on fromSite |
| `activityIds` |  | integer list | Only these activities and resources, by course module id |
| `sectionIds` |  | integer list | Only these sections, by id, each with everything in it |
| `toSite` | ✅ | string | A site's name, as list_sites gives it |
| `toCourseId` |  | integer | An existing course on toSite to copy into |
| `toSectionId` |  | integer | Into toCourseId: every copied activity at the end of this section |
| `toAfterSectionId` |  | integer | Into toCourseId: copied sections as new sections after this one |
| `toCategoryId` |  | integer | A whole course only: a new course in this category on toSite, instead of toCourseId |

</details>

### `list_assignments` {#list-assignments}

**List a course's assignments**

List the assignments of a Moodle course: their ids (course module ids, for the other assignment tools), names, URLs, visibility and section. Takes the course id from list_courses.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer | The course's id, as list_courses gives it |

</details>

### `get_submissions` {#get-submissions}

**Get an assignment's submissions**

Get the participants' submissions to a Moodle assignment, a page at a time (limit participants, 25 by default, after skipping offset; more says whether there are others): who (an alias when the server pseudonymizes, else id and name), status (submitted; draft; new: a submission started but nothing in it yet; reopened; none: no submission at all), whether it needs grading, extensions, the participant's dates and, by default, the content (online text and file links; names and contact data in it redacted when pseudonymizing). Changes nothing, but Moodle logs it as the teacher viewing the grading pages, as it does for its own grader. Takes the assignment id from list_assignments.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (its course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `includeContent` |  | boolean | Include each submission's content: online text and file links (default true) |
| `limit` |  | integer | How many participants (25 by default, up to 200) |
| `offset` |  | integer | How many participants to skip first, in the grading table's order (0 by default) |

</details>

### `get_rubric` {#get-rubric}

**Get an assignment's grading criteria**

Read how an assignment is graded: simple (a grade or a scale), a rubric (criteria with their levels and scores) or a marking guide (criteria with their maximum score). The criterion and level ids are what grade_submission's fields take. Takes the assignment id from list_assignments; needs at least one participant.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |

</details>

### `set_rubric` {#set-rubric}

**Define an assignment's rubric or marking guide**

Define how an assignment is graded with a rubric (criteria, each with two levels or more: a definition and its score) or a marking guide (criteria, each with a short name, a description for students, one for markers and a maximum score, and the guide's frequently used comments), through Moodle's advanced grading editor, ready to use. Creates one where there is none and replaces the one there is, so its criterion and level ids change. Refused once anything has been graded with it: Moodle would regrade. Returns the definition as get_rubric gives it. Changes how students are graded: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `method` | ✅ | `rubric`, `guide` |  |
| `name` | ✅ | string | Its name, as the advanced grading page lists it |
| `description` |  | string | Its description (HTML) |
| `criteria` | ✅ | object list | In order |
| `comments` |  | string list | A marking guide's frequently used comments, in order |

</details>

### `grade_submission` {#grade-submission}

**Grade a submission**

Grade a participant in an assignment, as Moodle's grader does: a grade (simple grading), a rubric's levels or a marking guide's scores per criterion (ids from get_rubric) with remarks, feedback comments (HTML, when the assignment has them on), whether to notify the student, and any other grading field by name in fields. Takes the participant as get_submissions gives them: user (an alias) when the server pseudonymizes, else userId. Works with or without a submission. Returns the grade saved. Changes grades students may see: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `user` |  | string | The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userId` |  | integer | The participant's user id, when the server shows names |
| `grade` |  | string | The grade as text: a number within the range ("7.5"), or a scale item |
| `feedback` |  | string | Feedback comments (HTML); no aliases in it, since the student reads it |
| `notify` |  | boolean | Notify the student; Moodle's default when missing |
| `rubric` |  | object | A rubric's level per criterion: criterion id → level id, as get_rubric gives them |
| `guide` |  | object | A marking guide's score per criterion: criterion id → score |
| `remarks` |  | object | Remarks per criterion of a rubric or guide: criterion id → text; no aliases |
| `feedbackFiles` |  | string list | Absolute local paths of feedback files to return to the student |
| `workflowState` |  | `notmarked`, `inmarking`, `readyforreview`, `inreview`, `readyforrelease`, `released` | With the marking workflow on: the state to leave the submission in ("released" shows the student the grade) |
| `applyToGroup` |  | boolean | In a group assignment: give the same grade and feedback to the whole group |
| `fields` |  | object | Other grading form fields by name, e.g. a rubric's levels |

</details>

### `grant_extension` {#grant-extension}

**Grant an assignment extension**

Grant participants an extension of an assignment's due date until a date, as the assignment's extension form does (several at once). Takes them as get_submissions gives them: users (aliases) when the server pseudonymizes, else userIds. Moodle refuses a date before the due date. Confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `users` |  | string list | The participants' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userIds` |  | integer list | The participants' user ids, when the server shows names |
| `until` | ✅ | string | ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-03T23:59:00+01:00 |

</details>

### `set_workflow_state` {#set-workflow-state}

**Set the marking workflow state**

Set the marking workflow state of participants' submissions, as the grading table's bulk action does: "released" shows them their grades (notify tells them). Takes them as get_submissions gives them. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `users` |  | string list | The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userIds` |  | integer list | The participants' user ids, when the server shows names |
| `state` | ✅ | `inmarking`, `readyforreview`, `inreview`, `readyforrelease`, `released` |  |
| `notify` |  | boolean |  |

</details>

### `allocate_marker` {#allocate-marker}

**Allocate a marker to submissions**

Allocate a marker (someone who can grade; several where the assignment uses several per submission) to participants' submissions, as the grading table's bulk action does; Moodle leaves submissions past marking alone. Participants and markers as get_submissions gives them: aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | ✅ | integer | The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it |
| `users` |  | string list | The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userIds` |  | integer list | The participants' user ids, when the server shows names |
| `markers` |  | string list | The markers' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes |
| `markerIds` |  | integer list | The markers' user ids, when the server shows names |

</details>

### `list_question_banks` {#list-question-banks}

**List a course's question banks**

List the question banks of a course: its shared banks (usable by any quiz in the course) and the activities' own banks (a quiz's, usable only there). Returns their ids, which list_questions, import_questions and create_question take. On Moodle 4.x a course has one bank, its own, whose id is the course's.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |

</details>

### `list_questions` {#list-questions}

**List a bank's questions**

List a question bank's categories and the questions in them, category by category: id, name, type, status and category. A page at a time: limit questions (100 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Takes the bank id from list_question_banks.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it |
| `limit` |  | integer | How many questions (100 by default, up to 1000) |
| `offset` |  | integer | How many questions to skip first, category by category (0 by default) |

</details>

### `validate_gift` {#validate-gift}

**Check GIFT questions before importing them**

Check questions in GIFT before import_questions, without Moodle: each question split at blank lines as Moodle's importer does, with its type in Moodle's names, title, text and answers, and each problem with its line (a question Moodle can't read, a weight it doesn't take, a multiple choice with no right answer, a matching question with fewer than two pairs); ordering questions in their own GIFT (&#123;&#62;…&#125;) too, as Moodle exports them. Fix what it reports and check again; valid means Moodle should import every question.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `text` |  | string | The questions in GIFT |
| `file` |  | string | Or an absolute path to a local GIFT file |

</details>

### `import_questions` {#import-questions}

**Import questions into a bank**

Import questions into a question bank from GIFT or Moodle XML, given as text or as a local file, through the bank's import form: the way to add several at once. Moodle checks the whole file first: when it can't parse it, nothing is imported and its messages come back. Returns the questions created. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it |
| `format` | ✅ | `gift`, `xml` |  |
| `text` |  | string | The questions in that format |
| `file` |  | string | Or an absolute path to a local file in that format |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing |

</details>

### `create_question` {#create-question}

**Create a question in a bank**

Create one question in a question bank through its type's form, of any type: multichoice, truefalse, shortanswer, numerical, essay, calculated (simple and multichoice too), match, randomsamatch, drag and drop into text (ddwtos), onto an image (ddimageortext), markers (ddmarker), select missing words (gapselect), Cloze (multianswer, its answers in the text), ordering, description, and the plugins coderunner, formulas, gapfill and ddmatch where the site has them. Each type takes its own inputs, checked before Moodle. The text holds the type's places: [[1]] for ddwtos and gapselect, &#123;1:SHORTANSWER:=Paris&#125; for Cloze, [gaps] for gapfill, &#123;wildcards&#125; for calculated. For several, import_questions is faster. Returns the new question's id. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it |
| `type` | ✅ | `multichoice`, `truefalse`, `shortanswer`, `numerical`, `essay`, `calculated`, `calculatedsimple`, `calculatedmulti`, `match`, `randomsamatch`, `ddwtos`, `ddimageortext`, `ddmarker`, `gapselect`, `multianswer`, `ordering`, `description`, `coderunner`, `formulas`, `gapfill`, `ddmatch` |  |
| `name` | ✅ | string |  |
| `text` | ✅ | string | The question text (HTML) |
| `answers` |  | object list | Multichoice, shortanswer and numerical answers |
| `correct` |  | boolean | Truefalse: the right answer |
| `pairs` |  | object list | match, ddmatch: each question and its answer; an answer without a question is a distractor |
| `choose` |  | integer | randomsamatch: how many short-answer questions of the category it draws |
| `choices` |  | object list | ddwtos, gapselect: the choices [[1]], [[2]]… in the text name, by position |
| `image` |  | string | ddimageortext, ddmarker: the background image, an absolute local path |
| `drags` |  | object list | ddimageortext: the draggable items |
| `markers` |  | object list | ddmarker: the markers |
| `drops` |  | object list | ddimageortext, ddmarker: where the items or markers go |
| `items` |  | string list | ordering: the items, in the right order |
| `wildcards` |  | object list | calculated, calculatedsimple, calculatedmulti: each &#123;wildcard&#125;'s values; Moodle's 1 to 10 without them |
| `sets` |  | integer | Calculated types: how many sets of values (10 by default) |
| `coderunner` |  | object | coderunner (a plugin) |
| `formulas` |  | object | formulas (a plugin) |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing |
| `defaultMark` |  | number |  |
| `fields` |  | object | Any other field of the type's form, by name |

</details>

### `update_question` {#update-question}

**Change a question in a bank**

Change a question of a bank through its type's form, with create_question's inputs: only what's given changes (a list given, such as answers, pairs, choices, items, drags, markers, drops or a wildcard's values, replaces the question's). Saving makes a new version with its own id, the one returned, which quizzes using the latest version get from then on. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it |
| `questionId` | ✅ | integer | As list_questions gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `text` |  | string | The question text (HTML) |
| `answers` |  | object list | Multichoice, shortanswer and numerical answers |
| `correct` |  | boolean | Truefalse: the right answer |
| `pairs` |  | object list | match, ddmatch: each question and its answer; an answer without a question is a distractor |
| `choose` |  | integer | randomsamatch: how many short-answer questions of the category it draws |
| `choices` |  | object list | ddwtos, gapselect: the choices [[1]], [[2]]… in the text name, by position |
| `image` |  | string | ddimageortext, ddmarker: the background image, an absolute local path |
| `drags` |  | object list | ddimageortext: the draggable items |
| `markers` |  | object list | ddmarker: the markers |
| `drops` |  | object list | ddimageortext, ddmarker: where the items or markers go |
| `items` |  | string list | ordering: the items, in the right order |
| `wildcards` |  | object list | calculated, calculatedsimple, calculatedmulti: each &#123;wildcard&#125;'s values; Moodle's 1 to 10 without them |
| `sets` |  | integer | Calculated types: how many sets of values (10 by default) |
| `coderunner` |  | object | coderunner (a plugin) |
| `formulas` |  | object | formulas (a plugin) |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing |
| `defaultMark` |  | number |  |
| `fields` |  | object | Any other field of the type's form, by name |

</details>

### `delete_questions` {#delete-questions}

**Delete questions from a bank**

Delete questions from a bank, every version of each, as the bank's delete action does. Moodle doesn't delete a question a quiz uses: it hides it, and hidden lists those. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it |
| `questionIds` | ✅ | integer list | As list_questions gives them |

</details>

### `set_question_status` {#set-question-status}

**Set a question ready or draft**

Set a bank question ready (quizzes can use it) or draft, as the bank's status menu does.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `questionId` | ✅ | integer | As list_questions gives it |
| `status` | ✅ | `ready`, `draft` |  |

</details>

### `list_question_categories` {#list-question-categories}

**List a question bank's categories**

List a question bank's categories as its categories page shows them, parents before their subcategories: id, name, parent, description and how many questions are directly in each. The bank's hidden Top is the top-level ones' parentId. Takes managing the bank's categories (a teacher's).

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |

</details>

### `add_question_category` {#add-question-category}

**Add a category to a question bank**

Add a category to a question bank, at the top level or inside parentId, with an optional description (HTML). Returns the category. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |
| `name` | ✅ | string |  |
| `parentId` |  | integer |  |
| `description` |  | string |  |

</details>

### `edit_question_category` {#edit-question-category}

**Rename or move a question category**

Change a question bank's category: its name, description (HTML) or parent (moving it with its subcategories and questions; the bank's Top moves it to the top level). Only what is given changes. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |
| `categoryId` | ✅ | integer | The category's id, as list_question_categories gives it |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `description` |  | string |  |
| `parentId` |  | integer |  |

</details>

### `delete_question_category` {#delete-question-category}

**Delete a question category**

Delete a question bank's category: its subcategories move up to its parent; one with questions needs moveTo, the category its questions go to. Moodle keeps a bank's last top-level category. Confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |
| `categoryId` | ✅ | integer | The category's id, as list_question_categories gives it |
| `moveTo` |  | integer | Where its questions go, when it has any |

</details>

### `move_questions` {#move-questions}

**Move questions to another category**

Move questions of a bank into one of its categories, several at once; each keeps its id and versions. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |

**Export a bank's questions to a file**

Save a bank's questions, or a category's with its subcategories, to a local GIFT or Moodle XML file: each question's latest version, hidden ones left out, with their categories, so import_questions recreates them. validate_gift reads a GIFT export back.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |

| `bankId` | ✅ | integer | The bank's id, as list_question_banks gives it (on Moodle 4.x, the course's id) |
| `format` | ✅ | `gift`, `xml` |  |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | Only this category; the whole bank when missing |

</details>

List a quiz's questions as its edit page does, in order: each slot's page, question id, type (or random), name and mark. Teachers only.

**Add questions to a quiz**

Add questions to a quiz: bank questions by id (from list_questions) and/or random questions from a bank category, at the end or on a given page. A quiz that has been attempted can't change its questions: Moodle refuses. Returns the quiz's structure afterwards. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

| `page` |  | integer | The page to add them to; the last when missing |

</details>

### `edit_quiz_slot` {#edit-quiz-slot}

**Change a quiz question's mark or place**

Change one slot of a quiz: its maximum mark, and where it is (after another slot, 0 for first, and on a page), as the edit page does. After attempts, Moodle lets the mark change (it regrades them) but not the order. Returns the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |

| `slot` | ✅ | integer | The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it |
| `maxMark` |  | number |  |
| `moveAfter` |  | integer | Put it after this slot (0: first) |
| `page` |  | integer | The page to put it on |

</details>

### `remove_quiz_slot` {#remove-quiz-slot}

**Remove a question from a quiz**

Remove a slot from a quiz, as the edit page's delete icon does; the question stays in its bank. A quiz with attempts can't change its questions. Returns the quiz's structure. Confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `slot` | ✅ | integer | The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it |

</details>

### `set_quiz_pages` {#set-quiz-pages}

**Set a quiz's pages**

Set how a quiz's questions are split into pages: perPage questions a page (0 for all on one), as "Repaginate" does, or page breaks exactly after the slots in breaksAfter. Returns the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `perPage` |  | integer | Questions per page; 0 for one page |
| `breaksAfter` |  | integer list | Or: a page break after each of these slots, and nowhere else |

</details>

### `add_quiz_section` {#add-quiz-section}

**Add a section to a quiz**

Add a section heading to a quiz, starting at a slot (the first of its page: see set_quiz_pages), optionally shuffling its questions. Returns the new section's id and the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `firstSlot` | ✅ | integer | The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it |
| `heading` | ✅ | string |  |
| `shuffle` |  | boolean |  |

</details>

### `get_quiz_results` {#get-quiz-results}

**Get a quiz's results**

Read a quiz's attempts as its grades report shows them: per attempt the participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), state, dates, grade and the mark per question; with responses, also each answer given (redacted when pseudonymizing). A page at a time: limit attempts (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `responses` |  | boolean | Also the answer per question (default false) |
| `limit` |  | integer | How many attempts (50 by default, up to 500) |
| `offset` |  | integer | How many attempts to skip first, in the report's order (0 by default) |

</details>

### `get_quiz_statistics` {#get-quiz-statistics}

**Read a quiz's statistics**

Read a quiz's statistics report, which tells which questions work: the quiz's figures (attempts, averages, median, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, internal consistency, error ratio, standard error) and per question its facility index, standard deviation, weights, discrimination index and efficiency, dubious ones marked; a random slot's questions and variants each with their own; with responses, how often each response was given (one page read per question). Figures as the report shows them. attempts chooses which attempts count; recalculate clears what Moodle stored. Aggregates only: no person.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it |
| `attempts` |  | `highest`, `all`, `first`, `last` | The quiz's grading method by default |
| `recalculate` |  | boolean | Calculate again now, for attempts finished since |
| `responses` |  | boolean | Also each question's analysis of responses |

</details>

### `set_quiz_override` {#set-quiz-override}

**Set a quiz override for a participant**

Give a participant their own quiz settings, as the quiz's user overrides do: open and close dates, time limit in minutes, or number of attempts (0 unlimited); what isn't given stays the quiz's. Takes the participant as list_participants gives them. Confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id) |
| `user` |  | string | The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userId` |  | integer | The participant's user id, when the server shows names |
| `open` |  | string | ISO 8601 |
| `close` |  | string | ISO 8601 |
| `timeLimitMinutes` |  | integer |  |
| `attempts` |  | integer | 0 for unlimited |

</details>

### `list_questions_to_grade` {#list-questions-to-grade}

**List a quiz's questions to grade by hand**

List a quiz's questions that wait for grading by hand (essays…), each with how many to grade and the finished attempts whose answer needs it (by attempt id, with the participant as an alias when the server pseudonymizes). Read an answer with get_attempt_review; grade it with grade_quiz_question.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `quizId` | ✅ | integer | The quiz's id (course module id) |

</details>

### `grade_quiz_question` {#grade-quiz-question}

**Grade a quiz question by hand**

Grade one question of a finished attempt by hand, with a comment, as the review's "Make comment or override mark" does: an essay waiting for grading, or any question whose mark is overridden. The mark is in the question's points (0 to its maximum). Returns the attempt's grade afterwards when shown. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `attemptId` | ✅ | integer | As list_questions_to_grade gives it |
| `slot` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `mark` | ✅ | number |  |
| `comment` |  | string | No aliases in it, since the student reads it |

</details>

### `get_grader_report` {#get-grader-report}

**Get a course's grades**

Read everyone's grades in a course as the grader report shows them, in one group when given: its columns (grade items, categories, the course total) and a row per participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes) with their grades.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `group` |  | integer | Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups |

</details>

### `set_grade` {#set-grade}

**Set a grade in the gradebook**

Set a participant's grade in a grade item, as the gradebook's single view does: a manual item takes it; an activity's or a category's is overridden (until override false takes it off). Also feedback and excluding it from the totals. The grade as text: points ("7.5"), a scale item, or "none" to empty it. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `itemId` | ✅ | integer | The grade item, as get_gradebook_setup or get_grader_report gives it |
| `user` |  | string | The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes |
| `userId` |  | integer | The participant's user id, when the server shows names |
| `grade` |  | string |  |
| `feedback` |  | string | No aliases in it, since the student reads it |
| `override` |  | boolean | false: take an activity's or category's override off |
| `excluded` |  | boolean | Exclude it from the totals |

</details>

### `export_grades` {#export-grades}

**Export a course's grades to a file**

Save a course's grades into a local folder as Moodle exports them for a teacher: a spreadsheet (xlsx, ods), CSV or XML, with the items, group, display and feedback chosen. The file names every participant: only with names in clear (the server's student data level), since a file can't be pseudonymized.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `format` | ✅ | `xlsx`, `ods`, `csv`, `xml` |  |
| `destDir` | ✅ | string | An absolute local folder |
| `itemIds` |  | integer list | Only these grade items |
| `groupId` |  | integer |  |
| `display` |  | `real`, `percentage`, `letter` list |  |
| `feedback` |  | boolean | Include feedback |

</details>

**Get a course's gradebook setup**

Read how a course's grades are computed, as the gradebook setup page shows it: its categories (aggregation, weight, maximum) and grade items (category, maximum, weight). No one's grades.

| Input | Required | Type | Description |

| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |

</details>

**Add a manual grade item**

Add a grade item graded in the gradebook (not by an activity): out of maxGrade (Moodle's default 100) or on a scale, at the top level or in a category, optionally hidden from students. Returns it as the setup shows it. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |

| `maxGrade` |  | number |  |
| `scaleId` |  | integer | A scale instead of points |
| `categoryId` |  | integer | The category to put it in, as get_gradebook_setup gives it |
| `hidden` |  | boolean |  |

</details>

### `update_grade_item` {#update-grade-item}

**Update a grade item**

Change a grade item from get_gradebook_setup: move it into a category, set its weight (percent, overriding the automatic one) or a manual item's maximum grade (an activity's is set in the activity). Returns the item afterwards. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `itemId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `category` |  | integer | The category to move it into |
| `weight` |  | number | Percent |
| `maxGrade` |  | number |  |

</details>

### `delete_grade_item` {#delete-grade-item}

**Delete a manual grade item**

Delete a manual grade item and every grade in it. An activity's item goes with its activity, so it's refused. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<details className="tool-inputs">
<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `itemId` | ✅ | integer |  |

</details>

### `add_grade_category` {#add-grade-category}

**Add a grade category**

Add a grade category to a course's gradebook, at the top level or inside another, with its aggregation. Returns it as the setup shows it. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |

| `aggregation` |  | `mean`, `median`, `lowest`, `highest`, `mode`, `weighted-mean`, `simple-weighted-mean`, `mean-with-extra-credits`, `natural` |  |

</details>

**Update a grade category**

Change a grade category from get_gradebook_setup: its name, aggregation, weight in its parent (percent, overriding the automatic one), or move it into another category. Returns it afterwards. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `courseId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `categoryId` | ✅ | integer |  |
| `name` |  | string |  |
| `aggregation` |  | `mean`, `median`, `lowest`, `highest`, `mode`, `weighted-mean`, `simple-weighted-mean`, `mean-with-extra-credits`, `natural` |  |

Delete a grade category: Moodle moves what it held into its parent and deletes its total's grades; the course's own category can't be deleted. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

<summary>Inputs</summary>

| Input | Required | Type | Description |
